## Summary

The issue was in `_maybe_memory_map` in `pandas/io/common.py` (called by `get_handle`). A `BytesIO` buffer *has* a `fileno` attribute, so it passed the `hasattr(handle, "fileno")` guard and proceeded into the mmap branch — but calling `handle.fileno()` on an in-memory buffer raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` (with a `'fileno'` message), which propagated out to the caller.

Two changes:

1. **`pandas/io/common.py:1211`** — Wrapped the `mmap.mmap(handle.fileno(), ...)` call in a `try/except UnsupportedOperation`, re-raising as a `ValueError` whose message contains the required substring `"memory_map=True is only supported when reading from a file path"`, chained from the original error via `from err`.

2. **`pandas/io/common.py:26`** — Added `UnsupportedOperation` to the `from io import (...)` block.

Verified: `BytesIO` + `memory_map=True` now raises the `ValueError`, and reading from an actual file path with `memory_map=True` still works. No test files were touched.
